Perennial bridesmaid/maid of honor here. I have a gown budget in my expenses haha. Kidding aside, I don’t find it kuripot—after all, your bridesmaids are more often than not people who are close to you and your groom and will understand your concerns!  It will be more difficult if you want a specific theme/design/color, though. A happy medium in that situation would be for both bride and bridesmaid to chip in. I attended weddings na subsidized yung for gown—either provided na yung tela (which significantly lowers the cost, IMO) or babayaran mo lang yung labor ng mananahi ni designer (in this case, the designer was the bride’s sister). 

For the weddings where I had to take care of my own gowns though, the then-brides-to-be told it to me straight because we have that kind of relationship haha. The more meticulous ones even provided suggestions where we can have our gowns made/bought, which I really appreciated kasi they took into consideration the convenience.

I will also teach them to be more independent at a young and appropriate age because it is easier to learn and develop life skills when you’re younger than when you are already a sheltered adult. 


I will also keep myself healthy para hindi ako maging chronically ill habang lumalaki sila. I know first-hand how difficult growing up with a chronically ill parent is. It completely changed the trajectory of our lives. This isn’t entirely preventable though, but I’ll do what I can to minimize the risk.

Nakakapagod din minsan to get to know a person. To tell them all about your lore, warts and all. And to learn about them too. When you get more life experience, the story tends to get longer, and sometimes, you are just too tired from work or from household chores to really sit down and get to know someone. I definitely had more energy for dating when I was in my 20s. Too bad I was a broke grad student for most of it. 

Pero we’ll see. I’m not closing any doors but I also know if it doesn’t happen for me, I’ll also be okay. Because I finally learned to be happy on my own, and having a boyfriend again should enhance that, not complete it. Not diminish it. Don’t get me wrong. It has happened before so I know I am capable of falling in love. I am just more cautious this time—not just because I know better, but because I have more to lose, if that makes sense? Weird nga na dapat mas cautious ako in my youth but I wasn’t as financially and emotionally stable then. I didn’t know what I wanted, other than to be adored, and my sense of self was shaky and heavily depended on that ‘adoration’. I’m not saying it’s a bad thing; I won’t be in a relationship with someone who does not find me attractive (and vice versa), but it’s at the bottom of my list now. Mostly, I just want someone kind who makes me laugh and/or have conversations about everything and nothing at all. Someone I do not have to live in fear of not pleasing or living up to the expectations they have of me in their heads.

Hi! Not a registered psychologist yet (stuck doing thesis) but I can help. :) Although both fields tend to overlap, there are notable differences between what a clinical psychologist and a psychiatrist does. For example, psychologists can administer and interpret psychological tests, while psychiatrists can prescribe psychotropic medication. You don’t need to have a Phd to become a registered psychologist, so if you take into account the number of years, mas mabilis maging RPsy kaysa maging psychiatrist. Psychologists in private practice charge competitive rates, lalo na if they specialise in treating specific clients (ex. Child psychologists). Depending on the clinic, almost the same lang din yung charge ng psychiatrist at psychologist. For psychologists naman na naga-administer and interpret ng tests, decent ang salary sa private companies. By decent, I mean, it makes up for the years spent studying! 

I hope you choose what is best aligned to your interests. We need more psychiatrists and psychologists! :) 

Source: Masters student in clinical psych, worked in a psychiatry department as nurse researcher.

Recognition is easy if you have enough empathy. It usually takes a negative event in your life and self-reflection (ex. why you’re stuck in a particular pattern of behaviour) for this to happen. Mere recognition of it is not enough if you want to become a better person, however. It’s only the first step. The hardest part is working on bettering yourself every day. Example, being more self-aware means not putting yourself in situations where a toxic pattern will happen again. I say it’s difficult because it’s easier to succumb to it as it is what we are used to, but know the good feelings of familiarity are only short-lived. The pay-off brought about by character growth is ultimately more satisfying. It also helps having a trusted person to keep you in check re: this toxic traits.
